answer: A strong defense is stake-backed reputation: an agent must lock a deposit and accumulate verified, peer-attested work before it can earn rewards. Like a harbor that admits only ships with a logged voyage, the registry trusts only identities with a real history, each task recorded as a compact sonnet of evidence naming what was done and who checked it. A falcon-fast swarm of fresh clones still starts at zero, so creating thousands of fakes means funding and aging each one, and bad work forfeits the stake — making a Sybil flood expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
